note: Independently rejudged against the complete RFC 4271 Section 4.3 sentence: "The lower-order four bits of the Attribute Flags octet are unused. They MUST be zero when sent and MUST be ignored when received." AttributeCode.FlagsConflict examines only Optional and Transitive; validateAttributeFlags maps those declared conflicts to exact RFC 7606 handling. Reserved-bit ORIGIN/AS_PATH/NEXT_HOP input requires ActionNone, while the defined-high-bit controls require TreatAsWithdraw and AttrCode 1. The relay test and daemon CI additionally require the useful UPDATE on both general and route-server sockets; the send-side assertions satisfy the sentence's zero-on-send clause. The actual CI observation is receipt and relay, not a separate RIB-installation query; no direct installation claim forms part of this judgment. The explicit Unchanged leaf preserves all original flag/attribute/NLRI expectations. Coarse producer-disabling records are not claimed as selective reserved-bit mutations, and no new runtime result is asserted here.
